name: Intermediate Atrioventricular Septal Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Intermediate AVSD

criteria.description: Echocardiographic visualization of a common atrioventricular junction with a single atrioventricular valve and a defect involving the atrial and ventricular septa
Presence of a common atrioventricular valve with two orifices and abnormal leaflet morphology
Evidence of left-to-right shunting with volume overload of right atrium and ventricle on imaging or catheterization
Signs of congestive heart failure in infancy such as tachypnea, failure to thrive, or recurrent respiratory infections

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic evidence of the atrioventricular septal defect with common AV valve morphology and demonstration of shunting
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings supported by clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Common atrioventricular valve with single annulus
searchTerms: single valve between atria and ventricles
one valve instead of two in heart

pathognomonic.symptomName: Atrioventricular septal defect involving both atrial and ventricular septa
searchTerms: hole in both atrial and ventricular septa
heart septum defects in both chambers

common.symptomName: Congestive heart failure symptoms in infancy
common.notes: Includes tachypnea, diaphoresis, and feeding difficulties

common.symptomName: Systolic murmur due to turbulent flow across septal defects
searchTerms: heart murmur from blood flow turbulence
systolic murmur due to septal holes

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive in early childhood
searchTerms: failure to gain weight and height
signs of high blood pressure in lungs
irregular heart rhythms including AV block

occasional.symptomName: Hepatomegaly secondary to right heart failure
searchTerms: liver swelling due to right heart problems
blue skin from abnormal heart blood flow
cyanosis due to right-to-left heart shunt

rare.symptomName: Stroke or embolic events secondary to paradoxical embolism
searchTerms: embolic events due to paradoxical embolism

rare.symptomName: Endocarditis involving the common atrioventricular valve

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia in advanced cases
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating common AV valve and septal defects
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical assessment
genetic: Association with trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in some cases
other: Cardiac catheterization to assess hemodynamics and pulmonary pressures

distinguishingFeatures: Complete AVSD has a single common AV valve with a large atrial and ventricular septal defect
More severe valve regurgitation and earlier heart failure presentation
Partial AVSD has separate mitral and tricuspid valves with only an atrial septal defect
Less involvement of ventricular septum and milder symptoms

redFlags: Severe congestive heart failure unresponsive to medical therapy
Onset of complete heart block or advanced arrhythmias
references: Anderson RH, et al. The Atrioventricular Septal Defect: Morphology and Surgical Implications. Heart. 2019.
Moller JH. Congenital Heart Disease in Infants and Children. 2021.
